key_insight: The paper shows that large language models contain highly localized, task-specific functional subnetworks that can be selectively updated to reduce catastrophic forgetting during continual learning.
engineering_relevance: For AI systems in engineering workflows, this suggests a more resource-efficient way to adapt large models over long sequential training without broadly perturbing previously learned capabilities.
method: Use gradient-attribution profiling to identify cognition-associated functional subnetworks with low mutual overlap.
Route each training example to its corresponding subnetwork and restrict parameter updates plus optimizer states to those regions.
Train with the CiMEO continual-learning framework to localize plasticity and preserve pretrained representations.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate CiMEO on 1.4 million sequential instructions and report the best average performance across five generative benchmarks spanning programming, exam-style tasks, and mathematical reasoning.
watch_item: Subnetwork routing and localization depend on reliable attribution signals, so performance may be sensitive to task identification quality and implementation overhead in large-scale training.
paper_title: Functional Subnetwork Localization for Efficient Continual Learning in Large Language Models
